requirement:
The harness MUST stop retrying a completion request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` when the next attempt would
start more than one minute after the first of its consecutive transient
failures, including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point.
It MUST then fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts
and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.
rationale:
The tests adequately check `requirements.authoring.provider_backoff.limit`. I read `ProviderBackoff::retry` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/backoff.rs` only to understand the inputs. I took the expected behaviour from the requirement text.

**Obligation 1: stop once the next attempt would start more than one minute after the first consecutive transient failure, including when `Retry-After` passes that point.**
- `retrying_stops_once_a_request_has_failed_for_a_minute` (in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/providers.rs`) feeds repeated 429 `ThrottlingException` failures at simulated times.
  - It asserts that no accepted wait ever moves the clock past `start + 60s`.
  - It asserts that the sequence eventually stops after more than 3 waits.
- The same test covers the boundary two ways:
  - A failure at 58s is allowed to wait up to 2s, so a start at or before the minute is accepted.
  - A `Retry-After` of 60 waits exactly 60s, and one of 61 stops. Together these pin the "more than one minute" edge from both sides.
- A `Retry-After` of 90 stops at once, which covers the clause about a provider delay passing the limit.
- The timeout kind (`TimedOut`, a request with no response) is also exercised as a transient failure in the last-failure cases.
- A permanent 400 `ValidationException` stops with its own error rather than the "kept failing" message, so the limit applies only to transient retries.
- The end-to-end test `a_request_failing_for_a_minute_fails_the_assessment` (in `src/authoring/mod.rs`) uses a provider that always returns 503. It runs under paused time and asserts that:
  - elapsed time stays within `RETRY_LIMIT`;
  - more than 3 attempts were made;
  - the assessment returns an error, via `unwrap_err`;
  - the usage log is consistent (`retried` is false on the final request).

**Obligation 2: fail with an error naming the attempt count and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.**
- In the unit test, the message must contain "kept failing for a minute", "after {attempts+1} attempts", and "HTTP 429 ThrottlingException". The count is computed from the loop, so it is checked against the real number of attempts.
- The "when available" cases are covered separately. Status only gives "last failure: HTTP 503". Code only gives "last failure: ThrottlingException". Neither status nor code gives the timeout text. Each case also asserts that the returned error has kind `TimedOut`.
- The end-to-end test asserts the exact text "after {attempts} attempts; last failure: HTTP 503 ServiceUnavailableException", where `attempts` is the number of requests the provider actually received.

**Other points.**
- "Consecutive" is handled by creating a fresh `ProviderBackoff` per completion request. The reset after a success is the parent `requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` obligation, not part of the limit.
- Randomised jitter does not make the assertions flaky. The assertions hold for any jitter value in the permitted range.

I found no untested obligation or weak assertion, and no `{fixme}` acknowledgments apply.

text: :::{req} provider_backoff.limit
The harness MUST stop retrying a completion request under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff` when the next attempt would
start more than one minute after the first of its consecutive transient
failures, including when a provider `Retry-After` delay would pass that point.
It MUST then fail the assessment with an error naming the number of attempts
and the last failure's HTTP status and provider error code, when available.
:::{req} provider_backoff
When a provider reports a transient failure, the harness MUST wait and retry
the same completion request. Transient failures are throttling, reported
through HTTP 429 or a Bedrock `ThrottlingException`; temporary unavailability,
reported through HTTP 500, 502, 503, or 504 or a Bedrock
`ServiceUnavailableException`, `InternalServerException`, or
`ModelNotReadyException`; and a request with no response after ten minutes,
which the harness MUST abandon. The retry MUST retain its prompt, history,
tools, and pending inputs. It MUST NOT
restart the assessment or repeat already completed tool calls. A permanent
input/context-length error, authentication failure, or invalid request MUST
remain an error; mentioning tokens in an error message alone MUST NOT trigger
retries.
The backoff window MUST start at one second and double after each consecutive
transient failure, up to sixty seconds. Each delay MUST be randomly selected
between half and all of that window to spread parallel retries. An available
provider `Retry-After` value, in seconds or HTTP-date form, MUST be honored as a
minimum delay even when longer than the window. A successful response MUST reset
backoff for the next completion request, and interruption MUST cancel both the
wait and further retries.
Each attempt MUST count toward the assessment totals under {cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_requests`.
Hidden SDK retries MUST remain disabled so the harness can account for attempts.
Transient retries MUST NOT be reported as finished judgments or terminal
assessment errors while recovery is still in progress. Pending inputs MUST be
recorded as evidence only after the request succeeds.
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider` {cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`
